next_question: Is the 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal on the 12-state SPA primarily Markov (action determines next state given current state, requiring only current-state conditioning) or genuinely beyond-Markov (history K>2 adds predictive information beyond current state)? Compare state-history K2 PMI (0.933 bits) against action-history K3 PMI (1.221 bits) at N=5000 on the same SPA: if K3 >> K2, signal is primarily Markov; if K2 is comparable to or exceeds K3 after history conditioning, beyond-Markov structure is demonstrated. This decomposition does not require null centering (it is a ratio/comparison, not an absolute test) and resolves the interpretive ambiguity without resolving the null bias problem.
why_next: All three materially orthogonal null frameworks (parametric bootstrap 0.357, Miller-Madow 0.407, conditional entropy -0.814) fail to center PMI null at zero for the 12-state hash-routed SPA at N=5000. The convergence (range 0.060 bits) confirms the bias floor ~0.36-0.42 bits is intrinsic to PMI weighted averaging across deterministic/stochastic strata, not estimator choice or permutation scheme. Null centering may be fundamentally impossible for this SPA class without modifying the SPA design (e.g., eliminating deterministic strata). The 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal remains reproducible but uninterpreted: is it Markov (action determines next state given current state) or beyond-Markov (history adds information beyond current state)? The action-history K3 PMI (1.221 bits) at same N provides a direct comparison that does not require null centering — it is a ratio/comparison between two PMI measurements, not an absolute significance test. This pivot is the highest-information next step given the null centering impasse.

do_not_assume: C-WEB-DYNAMICS is globally false. The 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal is real and reproducible (p=0.001). The FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING verdict is due to null methodology limitation, not absence of signal.
Null bias is evidence against beyond-Markov signal. The permutation bias is intrinsic to PMI estimator weighting; the p-value remains a valid significance test.

All PMI null frameworks are exhausted. The three tested frameworks share structural dependence on PMI weighted averaging; truly orthogonal frameworks (e.g., Bayesian model comparison, likelihood ratio tests, or non-PMI information-theoretic quantities on stochastic SPAs) are untested.

The 0.933-bit K2 PMI demonstrates beyond-Markov dynamics in the C-WEB-DYNAMICS sense (predictive structure beyond memory). The test is I(url_after; action | url_before, prev1, prev2) without history-conditioned baseline comparison. Action-history K3 (1.221 bits) at same N is higher, suggesting signal may be primarily Markov.
Production SPA results generalize from this simulation. The 12-state SPA has 12 states, 4 deterministic candidates, hash-based selection, no anti-bot/auth/visual complexity.
The bias floor of ~0.41 bits at N=5000 is irreducible. Alternative estimators, larger N, or different SPA designs may reduce it.

recommended_action: Design a signal decomposition experiment to determine whether the 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal is Markov or beyond-Markov. Compare state-history K2 PMI (0.933 bits) against action-history K3 PMI (1.221 bits) at N=5000 on the same 12-state SPA. Use a history-conditioned baseline: compute I(S_next; action | S_current, H_K) for K=1 (marginal), K=2 (current state), K=3 (current + 1 prior) to determine whether additional history beyond current state adds predictive information. If K3 > K2 by > 0.1 bits with valid comparison, beyond-Markov structure is demonstrated. If K3 ≈ K2 or K3 < K2, signal is primarily Markov (action determines next state given current state). This decomposition does not require null centering — it is a ratio/comparison between PMI measurements, not an absolute significance test. Also test at N=50000 to determine whether bias floor is finite-sample or asymptotic. If bias decreases with N, larger N may eventually enable valid null centering.
